note:
v12 (2026-10-26): a slot code and an interval word are one instruction (P162-P164). '0-0-1 weekly' names the hours AND the interval; capturing the code alone made a correct weekly methotrexate or vitamin-D course read as a daily never-event, which is the false positive that trains a reviewer to wave the queue through. Both planes now compose the pair, and P164 pins that composing it does not excuse an interval shorter than the label allows. v11 (2026-10-26): one unit law for strengths, and the never-event that table could not state (P156-P161). Perception was stamping ' mg' on every trailing brand number, which turned Thyronorm 50 into 50 mg of levothyroxine and Calcirol 60K into 60 mg of cholecalciferol; the unit of a bare number now comes from the formulary row's molecule in the deciding plane, a label that prints its own unit always wins, and 25 ratio brand labels match against either component. Two verdict-affecting rules were unreachable through that invented unit: the look-alike/different-strength guard (a tenfold mis-read that lives inside the brand name never reached the strength field, so 'Thyronorm 500' verified cleanly against a row the prescription never named), and the interval mandate table, which is keyed on mg and so could not describe the 60,000 IU weekly sachet at all — a month of daily 60,000 IU passed in both planes. Relabels in this version move toward the stricter verdict; P156/P158/P159 are the negative controls that prove the fix is not a blanket block. v10 (2026-10-26): the harm a combination brand carries is documented on the combination (P150-P155). Shared, versioned cross-engine conformance corpus (ADR-0012 / MED-015). Both the Python and TypeScript planes read THIS file, so there is exactly one golden set and neither tier can drift against a private copy. Cases are curated human prescription lines (not RX-* fixtures); sources for every rule they exercise are recorded per row in data/interactions.csv and data/contraindications.csv. v9 (2026-10-26): an ingredient-name guess is not a formulary match (P149). v4 (2026-10-25): the interval law. v3 labelled eight oral-methotrexate lines (P44, P45, P55, P56, P62, P63, P64, P65) merely 'interaction'. They dose a weekly-only drug daily or worse, which is an ISMP high-alert never-event, and 'interaction' is a verdict a plan can be built from. They are confirm_queue now; the interaction findings they were labelled for are still asserted via expect_finding and still fire, so the relabelling is an escalation, not a replacement. v3 held no interval-frequency cases at all; P111-P118 pin the law on both sides (weekly MTX passes, daily MTX queues) so a future scheduler that collapses 1/7 into one-slot-per-day fails the corpus instead of shipping.

v5 (interval-law reach): the interval *rules* were mirrored across the two planes but the raw-line *vocabulary* that feeds them was not, and neither list carried the plain English prescriptions are written in. Three lines were measured divergent or blind before this version: "every other day" queued a methotrexate never-event in the TS plane while the Python plane read no frequency and passed it; "every 3 days" did the reverse; and "daily" — the single most common way an oral-methotrexate fatal schedule is written — carried no frequency in either plane, so no interval rule could fire. Both planes now read one ordered token list (LINE_FREQ_TOKENS, mirrored verbatim) plus prose day/week/month and hourly forms, and this version pins one case per token class. The negative controls (once weekly, q 3 weeks, Q2W) and the plain-English daily lines for paracetamol and levothyroxine are in the corpus so the fix cannot silently become a blanket block. P133/P134 also retire the last entry on the runner's documented non-case list: a frequency the law cannot read IS reachable from a raw line ("Q5H" — five hours does not divide a day; "every 999 days" — a legible shape carrying a nonsense value), so the queue rule for a stated-but-unreadable code is now a cross-engine case rather than a per-tier unit test.

v6 (dose-cap law and its ceiling's provenance): the aggregate daily-cap rule was the last verdict-affecting rule that existed in only one plane. 'Tab Cetzine 10 BD x 5 days' (20 mg against a 10 mg licensed maximum) verdicted interaction in the TypeScript tier and pass in the Python tier. The three caps tables also disagreed: two engine literals and one sourced CSV that no code read, conflicting on 17 molecules including theophylline (450 vs a level-guided 900, which made a routine 800 mg/day modified-release course read as a fatal overdose in P42) and ondansetron (32 = a withdrawn IV figure, vs 24 oral). One table of record now, generated to both tiers, with a `basis` and an `escalate` flag: a cap the engine cannot verify for THIS patient — level-guided, weight-based, specialist-supervised — advises and never blocks. P41/P89 relabel because the bug they were masking is a different-strength misread: the guard's magnitude test threw away every bare decimal under 2 mg, blinding it to Alprax 0.5 and Digoxin 0.25, the sub-2 mg class where a tenfold error is fatal. P81 gains expect_not_finding: applying one stated strength to every molecule of a combination brand invented 380 mg/day of atorvastatin on a statin+aspirin line, and only a negative assertion pins that the number stopped being made up.

v7 (the second cap figure and the ceiling the patient lowers): labels carry two numbers for several molecules — a self-care figure under a prescription maximum — and the rule executed only the top one, so an ibuprofen course at 1600 mg/day stopped saying anything at all once the blocking ceiling moved to 2400. `advisory_mg` keeps the lower figure as a warn-only threshold. `lowered_by` does the same for the ceiling a declared condition lowers: paracetamol 2000 mg/day under liver disease, citalopram 20 under 65 or hepatic impairment, tramadol and tapentadol in renal impairment — all figures already sitting in the curated notes, none of them executed. The engine's excuse for level-guided drugs is that it has no serum level; it does not apply to a number the patient declares, so those lines are measured against the lower ceiling and the escalation law runs on it. v8 (one identity per drug): a drug has exactly one name in every table the engine indexes by, so a documented rule cannot be unreachable because of a spelling. The corpus gained P148 (lithium/pregnancy, ABSOLUTE, filed under the identity the strip does not print) and P31 was relabelled on measurement — the 325 mg iron ceiling became reachable from every ferrous sulfate brand, so a 500 mg/day course now queues in both planes where it passed in both. Relabels move toward the stricter verdict, never away, and every one carries the measurement that forced it.

The line names an ingredient, not a brand, and no formulary brand key contains 'ferrous sulfate' — 7 of the 583 molecules in the catalog are in that position. The web tier guessed a brand from its molecule index at 0.85 and then counted the guess as a formulary match, so a 0.97 reading of this line auto-passed a drug identity that nothing confirms; the API tier's normalize() returns None for the same line and queues it. One engine, one answer.

Chelation of ciprofloxacin by the iron in a haematinic is written against 'ferrous ascorbate+folate'; the iron-folate tablet is one of the most prescribed combinations in the catalog and was screened as two names that appear in no row. documented at combination granularity, with no component-level counterpart for the same partner: 89 of the 176 rows keyed on a whole combination are in that position, and a screening walk that names only components cannot reach any of them from any brand pair in the catalog.

A bare brand number takes its unit from the formulary row's molecule, not from a default. Perception used to stamp ' mg' on every trailing digit, which turned the catalog row 'Thyronorm 50' into 50 mg of levothyroxine against a 0.3 mg/day cap: a thousandfold over-read of a 50 mcg tablet, and a routine correct course that queued. This case pins the other direction — the clean read must pass.

cases.expect_finding: 10x difference in the brand name itself
cases.why: The tenfold mis-read hides inside the brand name. The line states no unit, the substring resolver answers with the row 'Thyronorm 50', and the strength is then read back from THAT row — so the line-vs-formulary comparison saw a perfect agreement with a label the prescription never wrote, and 500 mcg of levothyroxine passed. The line's number is now anchored to the resolved brand core, so the contradiction is the finding. Same guard as the stated-strength class, reached from a different field.

lines: Tab Amoxicillin+Clavulanic acid 500/125 BD x 5 days
cases.why: 25 catalog rows state one strength per component. Reading only the trailing half as *the* brand strength made a correct 500 mg amoxicillin line look fourfold wrong; a ratio label now matches against either component.

lines: Cap Calcirol 60K once weekly x 8 weeks
cases.why: The kilo-suffix brand number is the 60,000 IU sachet, not 60 mg. Reading it as a mass dropped both the multiplier and the unit the preparation is sold in. The weekly course is the label's own schedule, so it must pass — the negative control for the IU interval mandate below.

An interval mandate written in IU: 60,000 IU of cholecalciferol daily for a month is 1.8 million IU, and the vitamin-D toxicity that follows is the reason the label says once weekly. The mandate table could not express it — every row is keyed on mg, and an IU strength has no mg equivalent, so the caps and the interval rules both abstained and the schedule passed silently. The threshold is the dose size, so the 400-2,000 IU daily drops and syrups a patient legitimately takes are untouched.

The same mandate reached from the other two reading defects: the brand's 'D3' is a vitamin letter, not a 3 mg strength (the lookbehind keeps it out of the strength slot), and here the line states 60000 IU itself, so the unit comes from the label rather than from the molecule. Both planes must queue the daily schedule.

A slot code and an interval word on one line are ONE instruction — which hours, and how often that day comes around. The extractor kept only the code, so '0-0-1 weekly' arrived as a daily schedule and the IU mandate queued a correct eight-week course. The sealed fixture RX-038 is written this way, which is how the pair was measured.

A false positive here is not neutral — it teaches the reviewer to wave the queue through.

lines: Cap Calcirol 60K 1-0-1 alternate day x 8 weeks
cases.why: The qualifier composes, it does not excuse: 60,000 IU on alternate days is still three times the label's weekly maximum, so the mandate must bite at interval 2 as well as interval 1. The negative control for P162/P163.
